assertions.limitations: Invariant semantics (reported as required, with file/line refs): verifyDayInvariants (oracle.ts:49-331) does run after every step and labels its checks I1-I8, but the labels do not match architecture.md §1.2. It checks: I1-labeled = booking/booking and hold/booking table overlap (oracle.ts:263-300); I2-labeled = party size within table/combo bounds (:111-155); I3-labeled = booking has assigned tables/tables active (:84-107); I4-labeled = booking does not overlap a block (:302-325); I5 = hard-locked booking tables unchanged vs the previous step (:202-227, matches architecture); I6-labeled = guest pacing caps (:229-261); I7-labeled = channel/table-mode allowed (:125-175); I8-labeled = valid interval + guest service window (:77-82, :179-199). Consequently architecture I3 (online never borrows), I6 (atomic modify), I7 (search->hold agreement) and I8 (monotonic release) are not verified by the property suite at all, and I1's experience-cap branch and I4's 'expired hold consumes nothing' are not verified. Pacing is never exercised because pacingRules is always [] (arbitraries.ts:180), table modes are never exercised because serviceTableModes is always [] (:181), day scenarios never contain holds (:245), overbooks or special days, and the probe channel is always 'online'. The per-step sequence test has no oracle comparison; oracle agreement is per-scenario only, and the oracle is bounded to 2 swaps, matching the engine's own repair depth. If the parent reads 'I1 through I8' per architecture.md §1.2, this assertion is only partially covered (4 of 8 missing) and should be treated as a partial-coverage failure; the executed tests, budgets, export and oracle agreement all pass as reported. Also note the scale test asserts the status string 'no_fit' (underscore) while the contract quotes "no fit".
